name: Clomiphene monotherapy for low T

card.summary: Taking clomiphene alone to raise the body's own testosterone, pursued for muscle, fat-loss and appearance benefits tied to higher testosterone.
card.note: Prescription drug used off-label in men; visual disturbances and estradiol rises are reported.

quick.overview:
Clomiphene is a prescription selective estrogen receptor modulator that blocks estrogen feedback in the brain, increasing LH and FSH and so stimulating the testes to make more testosterone. Using it alone for low testosterone is an alternative some men and clinicians choose to testosterone replacement.

The appearance chain is higher testosterone, then more muscle, less fat and better energy for training. In hypogonadal men clomiphene has raised testosterone roughly two- to two-and-a-half-fold, and a registered phase 2 study followed 48 men for a year.
quick.how: It is taken by mouth under a prescriber's direction, with blood testosterone monitored. Online communities discuss it as an option that keeps the testes active compared with exogenous testosterone.
quick.risks: Reported effects include vision changes, headache and hot flashes, and estradiol rises alongside testosterone. It is prescription-only in the US, UK and Australia and is prohibited in sport. Use for men is off-label.

lead: Clomiphene (clomifene, Clomid) is a nonsteroidal selective estrogen receptor modulator. In men with low testosterone it is sometimes used off-label alone, without testosterone injections, to raise the body's own production.[1] Enthusiasts discuss it as 'clomid monotherapy'.

It acts at the hypothalamus, blocking estradiol's negative feedback, increasing GnRH pulses and raising LH and FSH.[1] Clomiphene is a mix of enclomiphene and zuclomiphene; enclomiphene is the pro-androgenic isomer.[1]

Wikipedia reports that in hypogonadal men it has raised testosterone about 2 to 2.5 times; in one study of men under 400 ng/dL, levels rose from 309 to 642 ng/dL over three months.[1] A phase 2 open-label one-year hypogonadism study with 48 men is registered.[2]

chain: Clomiphene blocks estrogen feedback in the brain
LH and FSH rise, increasing testicular testosterone
Higher testosterone supports muscle gain, lower fat and training drive
angle.text: Users pursue clomiphene to restore testosterone without replacement therapy, expecting body-composition and energy benefits.

paras: Clomiphene was synthesized in 1956 by the William S. Merrell Chemical Company and approved in the US in 1967 as Clomid for female infertility.[1] Use in men is off-label.[1]
In normal men, 50 mg/day for eight months raised testosterone more in younger men (about 870 ng/dL) than in older men (about 490 ng/dL), with estradiol also rising.[1]
Reported effects include vision changes, headaches, hot flashes and possible liver abnormalities; rare reports include raised triglycerides and reversible hair loss.[1]
It is prescription-only in the US, UK and Australia, prohibited by WADA under S4, and can appear undeclared in black-market products.[1]
ClinicalTrials.gov lists NCT01386567, a completed phase 2, one-year open-label study of treatment for hypogonadism in 48 men who had completed an earlier study (ZA-203), begun July 2011.[2]
